questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: Which pitch must be sharpened when constructing the G major scale?

C sharp

questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Creative Arts and Sports
questions.subStrandTitle: Components of Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: In a picture, what does dominance mainly mean?

Blue and violet

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: A learner wants one bottle in a still life to dominate the picture. Which choice best achieves this?

Making every object exactly the same size
Hiding the bottle behind all other objects

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: Which practice keeps the painting area hygienic after a still life lesson?

Leaving open paint containers on desks

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: Which judgement best analyses dominance in a still life painting?
options: The large orange calabash draws the eye first because it contrasts with the blue cloth

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: What does the time signature 3/4 tell a musician?
options: There are three crotchet beats in each bar
There are four crotchet beats in each bar
There are three bars in the whole song
There are four players in a group
questions.correctAnswer: There are three crotchet beats in each bar
questions.explanation: In 3/4 time, each bar has three beats and the crotchet receives one beat.
questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports
questions.learningOutcome: Describe 3/4 time in music.

questions.prompt: Which rhythm pattern correctly fills one bar of 3/4 time?
options: Minim plus crotchet
Semibreve plus crotchet
Four crotchets
Two minims
questions.correctAnswer: Minim plus crotchet
questions.explanation: A minim has two beats and a crotchet has one beat, making three beats in total.
questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports
questions.learningOutcome: Group notes in 3/4 time.

questions.prompt: Which French rhythm names fit a bar containing a crotchet followed by a pair of quavers and another crotchet?
options: Taa, ta-te, taa
Taa-aa-aa-aa only
Ta-te, ta-te, ta-te, ta-te
Taa-aa, taa-aa
questions.correctAnswer: Taa, ta-te, taa
questions.explanation: A crotchet is spoken as taa and a pair of quavers as ta-te, giving three crotchet beats in the bar.
questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports
questions.learningOutcome: Perform four-bar rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names.

questions.prompt: Why should bar lines be inserted when writing a four-bar rhythm in 3/4 time?
options: They separate groups of three beats so the rhythm is clear
They make the notes louder automatically
They show the colour of the instruments
They replace the need to count beats
questions.correctAnswer: They separate groups of three beats so the rhythm is clear
questions.explanation: Bar lines organise the rhythm into equal measures according to the time signature.
questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports
questions.learningOutcome: Compose a four-bar rhythmic pattern in 3/4 time.

questions.prompt: A group claps a rhythm but one bar has four crotchet beats in 3/4 time. What should they do?
options: Remove or change one beat so the bar totals three beats
Clap louder to hide the extra beat
Add another bar line after every note
Change the title of the rhythm only
questions.correctAnswer: Remove or change one beat so the bar totals three beats
questions.explanation: Every bar in 3/4 time must add up to three crotchet beats.
questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse rhythmic patterns in 3/4 time for accuracy.

questions.prompt: Which choice best describes a strong four-bar rhythm composition task?
options: It keeps three beats per bar and uses varied note values that can be clapped clearly
It has random notes with no time signature
It repeats one mistake in every bar
It uses pictures instead of rhythm notation only
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps three beats per bar and uses varied note values that can be clapped clearly
questions.explanation: A good rhythm in 3/4 time is organised, performable, and rhythmically varied.
questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports
questions.learningOutcome: Create and perform a four-bar rhythm in 3/4 time.

questions.prompt: Which races are commonly described as middle distance races at this level?

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: Which safety action is important before practising middle distance running?

questions.explanation: A warm-up and a clear running space reduce injuries and collisions during practice.
questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety while practising middle distance races.

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: In melody writing, what is an answering phrase?

A painting technique for fabric
A movement used to mark an opponent
A type of race finish
questions.correctAnswer: A phrase that responds musically to an opening phrase
questions.explanation: An answering phrase completes or responds to the musical idea introduced by an opening phrase.

questions.prompt: Which notes belong to the G major scale used in Grade 8 melody work?

G, A, Bb, C, D, Eb, F, G
C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C
A, B, C, D, E, F, G, A

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.prompt: Which method extends a melody by repeating the same notes and rhythm?

Stencil printing
Overarm service
Water treading

Copying every note exactly
Ignoring the time signature
Changing the task into a drawing
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping the opening rhythm but changing some pitches within G major
questions.explanation: Varied repetition keeps a recognisable idea while changing some details to add interest.
questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

questions.strandTitle: Creating and Performing in Creative Arts and Sports

Pivoting
Marbling
Tagging

Only team scores
Only fabric dye recipes
Only middle distance race times
